claims.text: The nominal Ti35Ni35Co15Fe10Mo5 alloy is a Ti–Ni-primary high-entropy alloy.
Conventional casting or arc melting can produce the nominal alloy with homogeneous elemental distribution.
Adding 0.5–1.0 at% carbon and applying solution treatment plus aging will form nanoscale carbide precipitates.
The precipitates formed by the intervention will be uniformly dispersed.
The carbide precipitates will primarily be TiC.
NiC may also form during the proposed treatment.
Solution treatment at approximately 1100°C will homogenize the carbon-containing alloy.
Aging at 900°C for 4 hours will precipitate nanoscale carbides without unacceptable coarsening or unwanted phase transformations.
Dispersed carbide precipitates obstruct dislocation motion.
Dispersed carbide precipitates pin grain boundaries.
Obstruction of dislocation motion by the carbide dispersion will impede dislocation glide at high temperature.
Carbide dispersion and grain-boundary pinning will impede diffusional creep at high temperature.
The carbon-added and aged alloy will have higher elevated-temperature yield strength than the baseline alloy.
The carbon-added and aged alloy will have a lower elevated-temperature creep rate than the baseline alloy.
Keeping carbon at 0.5–1.0 at% will avoid altering the alloy's phase stability.
The proposed mechanism is applicable across Ti–Ni-primary high-entropy alloys whose other constituents are each present at 5–35 at%.
The nanoscale carbide dispersion will remain sufficiently stable to improve properties during elevated-temperature testing.

contradictions.description: The baseline field excludes the carbide-promoting aging treatment, whereas the predicted-outcome language and falsification experiment call for a baseline processed identically to the carbon-containing alloy. These define materially different controls.

The boundary states that additional elements are present at 5–35 at% each, but the intervention introduces carbon at only 0.5–1.0 at%. Under the query's stated definition applying to every constituent, the modified composition falls outside the declared compositional boundary.
